patents.title: Single poly embedded eprom
patents.inventors: Ching-Sung Yang; Shih-Jye Shen; Ching-Hsiang Hsu
patents.coreProblem: Store charge in a single-poly cell without a control-gate programming bias.
patents.mechanism: Two series PMOS devices provide selection and floating-gate charge storage through hot-carrier injection.
patents.claimFocus: Claim 1 is a device claim: two series PMOS transistors, the specified select-gate/source-line/bit-line connections, a floating gate on the second transistor, and hot-carrier injection without a control-gate programming bias. Claim 1 does not specify the former draft’s 3–8 V range or negative drain bias.

patents.inventors: Ching-Hsiang Hsu; Shih-Jye Shen; Ming-Chou Ho
patents.coreProblem: Floating-gate doping and injected carrier polarity affect retention and must be considered with the cell structure.
patents.mechanism: A PMOS selector and a PMOS storage device with a P-doped floating gate share an N well; the disclosure relates doping to charge retention.

patents.title: Non-volatile memory array
patents.inventors: Yen-Tai Lin; Shih-Jye Shen; Ching-Sung Yang; Ching-Hsiang Hsu
patents.coreProblem: In large-scale arrays of single-poly floating-gate cells, capacitive cross-coupling between bit lines and source lines induces read disturb and parasitic crosstalk leakage.
patents.mechanism: Employs shared source lines and symmetrical virtual ground geometry, utilizing alternating bias switching to suppress charging and discharging of parasitic capacitances in unselected cells.
patents.claimFocus: Claim 1 recites an array architecture comprising a plurality of bit lines, word lines, and single-poly cells each including a select transistor and a floating-gate transistor, wherein adjacent columns share a source line and a low bias voltage is applied during read operations to suppress read disturb.

patents.title: Method for reading single poly 1T non-volatile memory cell
patents.inventors: Hsin-Ming Chen; Shih-Jye Shen; Ching-Sung Yang; Ching-Hsiang Hsu
patents.coreProblem: Conventional 2T cells occupy significant silicon area, whereas 1T single-transistor cells without dedicated selectors suffer from unselected leakage and over-erase conduction.
patents.mechanism: Leverages sub-micron channel weak-inversion sensing with dynamic source-drain bias reversal to achieve precise threshold voltage window discrimination on 1T cells, suppressing over-erase and unselected leakage.
patents.claimFocus: Claim 1 recites a method of reading a single-poly single-transistor memory cell by applying a read voltage to the gate and establishing a small sensing voltage differential between drain and source to determine binary states non-destructively based on channel conduction influenced by floating-gate stored electrons.

patents.title: Breakdown-Free Negative Level Shifter
patents.coreProblem: During high-voltage programming or erasing in non-volatile memories, negative voltage level shifters must transition between standard logic levels (e.g., 0V to 3.3V) and negative high-voltage rails (e.g., -5V to -10V), exposing cross-coupled MOS devices to excessive electric field stress exceeding gate oxide dielectric breakdown limits.
patents.mechanism: Introduces series-connected clamping and voltage-dividing structures between cross-coupled inverter pairs and input switching transistors, dynamically restricting maximum potential differences relative to substrate and wells within a single power supply tolerance to eliminate gate oxide overstress.
patents.claimFocus: Claim 1 defines a negative voltage level shifting circuit: comprising a pair of cross-coupled transistors, first and second input transistors, and breakdown protection circuitry configured to convert a first logic level to a second negative high-voltage level, wherein maximum voltages across all internal nodes remain substantially below predetermined oxide breakdown limits.

patents.title: Anti-fuse memory cell
patents.inventors: Meng-Yi Wu; Te-Hsun Hsu; Hsueh-Wei Chen; Ching-Hsiang Hsu
patents.coreProblem: Standard gate oxide antifuse breakdown produces unconstrained stochastic thermal filament rupture, causing wide post-breakdown resistance spread and localized silicon lattice cratering.
patents.mechanism: Introduces graded doped halo buffer wells and gate edge electric field modulation to confine dielectric breakdown to an engineered gate overlap edge, achieving low-voltage deterministic rupture.
patents.claimFocus: Claim 1 defines an antifuse memory cell comprising a substrate, a gate dielectric layer, and a conductive gate electrode forming an overlap region over a graded diffusion well, configured such that programming voltage induces localized oxide rupture exclusively at the predetermined edge region.

patents.coreProblem: High programming electric fields in antifuse arrays induce severe half-select gate dielectric stress and substrate punch-through in unselected cells along the same bitline.

litigationDefense.title: Claim Boundaries and Comparison Questions
litigationDefense.overview: The selected publications establish technical limitations. They do not establish litigation outcomes, infringement, invalidity or freedom to operate.

keyBattles.heading: NeoBit® Comparison: Single-Poly Floating-Gate OTP
keyBattles.detail: Claim 1 is a device claim: two series PMOS transistors, the specified select-gate/source-line/bit-line connections, a floating gate on the second transistor, and hot-carrier injection without a control-gate programming bias. Claim 1 does not specify the former draft’s 3–8 V range or negative drain bias.

keyBattles.heading: NeoFuse® Comparison: Antifuse OTP
keyBattles.detail: Claim 1 requires four doped regions in a well, complete well separation of the second and third regions, gate oxide, three spanning gates, and a metal bit line connected through two vias to the first and fourth regions. The scope is this combination, not every gate-oxide OTP.

keyBattles.heading: NeoEE® Comparison: Erasable Single-Poly NVM
keyBattles.detail: Claim 1 combines series cell rows, floating-gate transistors, program/control gates, row/column wiring and well-based erase lines. The floating gate spans three active regions; the storage transistor is P-channel and the program/control gates are N wells. A generic coupling capacitor is insufficient.

keyBattles.heading: NeoMTP® Comparison: Assistant-Gate Cells and Arrays
keyBattles.detail: Claim 1 requires two OD regions in an N well, a series PMOS selector and storage transistor on the first region, and an assistant gate extending from the floating-gate end to the second-region edge. N-well bias controls the coupled voltage; it is not a generic separate erase gate.

keyBattles.heading: NeoPUF® Comparison: Antifuse and Security Systems
keyBattles.detail: Claim 1 requires select, switching and antifuse transistors with specified control lines in each subcell, a connection circuit, a copying circuit containing a third antifuse, and readout that generates a random code from that third antifuse. An antifuse alone is insufficient.

patents.title: Write enhancement for one time programmable (OTP) semiconductors
patents.inventors: Harry Luan; Tao Su; Steve Wang; Charlie Cheng
patents.coreProblem: In advanced HKMG logic nodes, conventional unipolar single-pulse programming risks over-stressing unselected cells along bitlines and inducing soft breakdown degradation.
patents.mechanism: Applies an asymmetric bipolar dual-pulse programming sequence, coupling positive bias on select pass gates while applying negative voltage pulses (-1.0V to -2.0V) on the bitline to lower absolute positive voltage stress and stabilize filament rupture.
patents.claimFocus: Claim 1 recites a method of programming an OTP memory cell comprising applying a first programming pulse by setting a positive voltage on the pass transistor gate, a positive voltage on the programming gate, and a negative voltage on the bitline to rupture the dielectric layer, followed by a second pulse including negative voltage.

patents.title: Variable thickness gate oxide antifuse memory cell with geometric transition
patents.coreProblem: Abrupt perpendicular boundary steps between thick and thin gate oxides cause optical lithography distortion and localized mechanical stress, triggering parasitic breakdown in unselected cells.
patents.mechanism: A triangular or angled geometric transition boundary between thick and thin oxide regions smooths electric field gradients, confining breakdown current strictly within the geometric center and preventing parasitic fringe leakage.
patents.claimFocus: Claim 1 defines cell physical layout: comprising a first diffusion and gate structure, where the gate dielectric includes thick and thin oxide regions in layout view, with an interface boundary forming an angled or triangular geometry non-parallel to channel length to define breakdown filament nucleation.

patents.title: Low-Vt antifuse memory cell formed in high-voltage well
patents.coreProblem: As advanced nodes scale below 28nm with core VDD at 0.8V~0.9V while programming requires 5V~6V, placing antifuse cells in standard logic wells risks substrate punchthrough and junction breakdown.
patents.mechanism: Antifuse cells are isolated in dedicated high-voltage deep N-wells with threshold-adjust implants blocked from the channel, producing a low-Vt read channel combining high programming breakdown tolerance with enhanced read current drive.
patents.claimFocus: Claim 1 defines a memory structure: an isolated high-voltage well in a semiconductor substrate, an active region in the well, and a gate overlying the active region, wherein the channel omits threshold-voltage implants to exhibit lower Vt than core logic transistors, with the well terminal coupled to independent bias circuitry.

patents.title: High Speed OTP Sensing Scheme
patents.coreProblem: Single-ended antifuse memory cells exhibit post-breakdown conductive resistances spanning several kΩ to tens of kΩ with significant process variation, while unprogrammed cells exhibit negligible leakage; conventional voltage sensing is slow and susceptible to read disturb at elevated bitline voltages.
patents.mechanism: Employs a bitline-clamped low-impedance single-ended current sensing scheme coupled with a controlled current mirror reference and dynamic sensing nodes; clamps the bitline to a sub-volt low level during read to eliminate read disturb while a differential current comparator rapidly resolves binary logic states.
patents.claimFocus: Claim 1 defines a memory read sensing architecture: comprising a bitline coupled to an antifuse cell, a reference circuit supplying a dynamic reference current, and a current sense amplifier coupled to the bitline with a clamping transistor restricting bitline voltage to a low level during read cycles to prevent antifuse dielectric disturb.

patents.coreProblem: Traditional Fowler-Nordheim (FN) tunneling erasure in single-poly MTP cells requires >12V potentials and tens of milliseconds, straining on-chip charge pumps and causing oxide wearout.
patents.mechanism: Applies band-to-band hot-hole injection (BBHH) assisted by negative control gate bias, neutralizing floating-gate electrons under lower terminal voltages (<8V) within 10 milliseconds.

Excludes slow high-voltage Fowler-Nordheim positive tunneling schemes.

patents.title: Methods and Apparatuses for a Sense Amplifier in Non-Volatile Memory
patents.coreProblem: In dual-polarity embedded non-volatile memories, high-voltage programming pulses (e.g. 8V-10V) applied during STORE operations can catastrophically breakdown unprotected sense amplifier input nodes and critical switching transistors.
patents.mechanism: Integrates store protection circuitry and idling isolation within the sense amplifier, dynamically clamping potential differences across critical sensing nodes to within a safe margin between high store voltage and Vdd, while isolating current sources during idle mode to prevent leakage.

vendors.strategy: I-fuse uses heat-assisted electromigration within a controlled programming window. This dossier selects issued claims on reliable programming and non-destructive OTP testing; the connection to I-fuse is an editorial comparison with the company white paper, not a claim chart for any specific commercial macro. Programming changes fuse resistance; a pseudo-programmed test readout does not consume the OTP state.

families.name: I-fuse® Reliable Programming and OTP Testability
families.tagline: Controlled programming window · Non-destructive test readout
families.cellTopology: Electrical fuse, selector and read circuit; the white paper illustrates a 1R1D array.
families.physicalMechanism: Heat-assisted electromigration raises fuse resistance for storage. Low-bias concurrent write/read changes the sensed output during testing without changing the stored state.
families.processNode: Claims are not tied to a named node; the cited 2023 product announcement reports 12 nm FinFET silicon.
families.summary: Two issued publications are selected for complementary teaching topics: controlled fuse programming and testability. The collection is an editorial technology portfolio, not a complete patent family or portfolio. Material options in dependent claims do not establish production qualification at every node.

patents.title: Method and Structure for Reliable Electrical Fuse Programming
patents.assignee: Attopsemi Technology Co., Ltd. — assignee on the issued front page
patents.coreProblem: Excess current can cause abrupt resistance changes and a broad programmed-resistance distribution. A usable programming window must be characterized rather than treating any large current as reliable programming.
patents.mechanism: The disclosure uses a current threshold to separate controlled electromigration from disruptive programming. Claim 1 uses multiple pulses for progressive resistance change below the critical current. Independent claim 9 characterizes lower and upper programming bounds through read verification; it is a separate claim path.
patents.claimFocus: Claim 1 combines plural OTP cells, a fuse coupled to a first supply line, an enabled selector coupled to a second line, multiple voltage/current pulses that progressively change resistance, determination of a critical current causing drastic resistance change, and limiting programming below it. Claim 4 adds material choices including CMOS metal gate and metal interconnect. Claim 9 separately defines programming-window characterization. Claim 1 does not specify 0.4 V readout, automotive qualification or a process node.
patents.productLink: The claim-1 current limit and claim-9 program window align technically with the I-fuse white paper. This is editorial mapping; neither a universal claim on all non-explosive fuses nor proof that every I-fuse macro practices every element.

patents.title: Fully Testible OTP Memory
patents.assignee: Attopsemi Technology Co., Ltd. — assignee on the issued front page
patents.coreProblem: A blank OTP normally exposes only its virgin readout. Permanently programming test patterns consumes usable bits, so read circuits and addressing paths need an alternative way to exercise both readout states.
patents.mechanism: Low-voltage/current stimulus during reading creates a pseudo-programmed output while leaving the fuse state unchanged. Alternating normal and pseudo-programmed readouts permits test patterns. The company calls its implementation CLVWR; this is a test mode, not erase or multi-time storage.
patents.claimFocus: Claim 1 requires plural fuse-based OTP cells, a selector, a resistance-to-logic read circuit, and low-voltage/current test stimulus that changes read output without programming a different stored state. Dependent claim 2 adds an initial resistance below 400 ohms; claim 3 adds alternating virgin and non-destructive programmed readouts. Independent claim 13 covers alternating non-destructive readout test patterns. The 400-ohm condition is not mandatory in claim 1, and the claims do not guarantee zero defects.
patents.productLink: The patent abstract and claims match the low-bias pseudo-programmed readout described as CLVWR in the I-fuse white paper. A technical match does not establish a claim chart for a specific customer macro or validate every advertised coverage figure.

patents.title: OTP Memory with High Data Security
patents.assignee: Attopsemi Technology Co., Ltd. — Granted Patent Assignee
patents.coreProblem: Conventional fuses programmed with excessive current suffer rupture, melting, or thermal runaway, leaving visible physical damage readable via delayering or SEM/TEM, and causing large resistance spread.

patents.title: One-Time Programmable Memories with Ultra-Low Power Read Operation and Novel Sensing Scheme
patents.coreProblem: In IoT and edge AI computing chips, conventional DC read sensing in OTP consumes excessive static current, and continuous read voltages applied to antifuse or fuse microfilaments can induce low-field electromigration or resistance drift over time (read disturb).
patents.mechanism: Proposes a dynamic charge transfer and transient charge accumulation sensing topology utilizing minute parasitic or integrated capacitors for charge and discharge slopes; limits read bias across the I-fuse resistor to sub-microampere regimes to achieve near-zero static standby power and superior read immunity.
patents.claimFocus: Claim 1 defines a one-time programmable memory device: comprising a memory array of OTP cells each with a programmable resistive element and a selector; read control circuitry configured to restrict read voltage across the resistive element well below a programming threshold, and a dynamic charge sense amplifier determining logic states by comparing bitline discharge slopes.

litigationDefense.title: Claim Boundaries and Product Mapping
litigationDefense.overview: The selected publications support technical teaching, not a finding about a lawsuit or a blanket patent moat. The issued claims and company product disclosures serve different evidentiary purposes.

keyBattles.heading: Programming and Material Choices
keyBattles.detail: Claim 1 combines plural OTP cells, a fuse coupled to a first supply line, an enabled selector coupled to a second line, multiple voltage/current pulses that progressively change resistance, determination of a critical current causing drastic resistance change, and limiting programming below it. Claim 4 adds material choices including CMOS metal gate and metal interconnect. Claim 9 separately defines programming-window characterization. Claim 1 does not specify 0.4 V readout, automotive qualification or a process node.

keyBattles.heading: Test Readout and Stored State
keyBattles.detail: Claim 1 requires plural fuse-based OTP cells, a selector, a resistance-to-logic read circuit, and low-voltage/current test stimulus that changes read output without programming a different stored state. Dependent claim 2 adds an initial resistance below 400 ohms; claim 3 adds alternating virgin and non-destructive programmed readouts. Independent claim 13 covers alternating non-destructive readout test patterns. The 400-ohm condition is not mandatory in claim 1, and the claims do not guarantee zero defects.

litigationDefense.ftoVerdict: Current enforceability and freedom to operate are not determined here. Read the complete claim combination and relevant jurisdiction, prosecution history, maintenance and related rights. Product similarity alone does not establish infringement.

patents.title: Multilevel Floating Gate Sensing Circuit
patents.coreProblem: When implementing Multi-Level Cell (MLC) storage in split-gate flash memories, conduction current differences between adjacent programmed states are extremely minute, making conventional binary sense amplifiers incapable of reliably differentiating multiple stored levels in noisy environments.
patents.mechanism: Introduces a two-stage sensing architecture pairing a first voltage amplifier with multiple current amplifiers and dummy reference cells, linearly translating minute split-gate cell currents into proportional currents and decoding them simultaneously into multi-bit digital signals with high noise immunity.

patents.title: Variable Charge Pump Circuit with Dynamic Load
patents.inventors: Angelo Bedarida; Carlo Maria Colle; Marco Sforzin
patents.coreProblem: During flash memory erase and program modes requiring diverse high voltage levels from on-chip charge pumps, rapid mode switching and load transients induce excessive voltage ripple and sluggish regulation that threaten dielectric integrity in tunnel oxides.
patents.mechanism: Architects a variable charge pump with multi-stage pumping and dynamic load regulation, utilizing multi-phase clocking and feedback dynamic biasing to switch active pump stages and capacitive paths according to transient loads, minimizing ripple while preserving high power-conversion efficiency.
patents.claimFocus: Claim 1 defines a charge pump circuit for generating a charge pump voltage with minimal voltage ripple: comprising a pumping circuit with one or more stages operable to receive a supply voltage and generate selected pump voltages, and a regulation circuit coupled to dynamically regulate pumping stages.

patents.title: Circuit and Method of Writing a Toggle Memory
patents.inventors: Joseph J. Nahas; Thomas W. Andre; Chitra K. Subramanian; Brad J. Garni
patents.coreProblem: In Toggle MRAM, identical write pulse sequences unconditionally rotate free-layer magnetic moments by 180 degrees; applying a write toggle when the targeted cell already holds the desired data state causes destructive overwriting and wastes significant dynamic write power.
patents.mechanism: Provides a write driver circuit with read-before-write and early pulse termination: initiating a read operation at the targeted address, concurrently initiating a preliminary portion of the write toggling sequence, and selectively terminating the toggle sequence prior to completion based on the read data state.
patents.claimFocus: Claim 1 defines a method for reading and writing a toggle memory: comprising initiating a read operation of a predetermined address location, initiating a portion of a write toggling operation during the read operation, and selectively terminating the write toggling operation before completion based on the data state read during the read operation.

patents.title: Low Forming Voltage OxRAM Memory Cell, and Associated Method of Manufacture
patents.inventors: Gabriel Molas; Thomas Magis; Jean-François Nodin; Alessandro Bricalli; Guiseppe Piccolboni; Yifat Cohen; Amir Regev
patents.assignee: COMMISSARIAT A L'ENERGIE ATOMIQUE ET AUX ENERGIES ALTERNATIVES; WEEBIT NANO LTD
patents.coreProblem: Conventional OxRAM requires an initial forming voltage significantly higher than nominal operating voltage (>4V), forcing larger peripheral selector transistors and hindering scaling density in embedded ReRAM macros.
patents.mechanism: Engineers a graded oxygen-reservoir upper electrode comprising a metal layer over a conductive sub-oxide (MOy) with electrical conductivity > 100 S/m, drastically lowering the forming voltage of a 40nm cell from 4.8V down to 2.0V.
patents.claimFocus: Claim 1 (Col 16, L56 to Col 17, L8) specifies an OxRAM cell: having lower and upper electrodes and an active insulating oxide layer for conductive filament formation, wherein the upper electrode includes an oxygen reservoir layer with an upper metal portion and a lower second oxide portion of the same metal that is conductive with conductivity > 100 S/m. Excludes standard ReRAM stacks having pure metallic reservoir layers without a conductive sub-oxide interface.

patents.title: Current and Voltage Limit Circuitry for Resistive Random Access Memory Programming
patents.coreProblem: During Forming/Set operations in ReRAM, sudden filament percolation creates transient current overshoot that over-thickens conductive filaments, severely degrading endurance and reset yield.
patents.mechanism: Integrates an active current and voltage limiter in the bitline write path with a fast-feedback clamp transistor that dynamically restricts peak transient current and terminal voltage on nanosecond timescales.
patents.claimFocus: Claim 1 (Col 7, L49 to L60) specifies a current and voltage limit circuit for RRAM programming: comprising a bitline clamping transistor coupled to a selected cell and dynamic bias logic configured to restrict maximum transient current and voltage across the cell during write pulses, maintaining thin, switchable filaments. Excludes passive fixed resistor dividing networks lacking active transient clamping.

patents.title: Method for Programming an Array of Resistive Memory Cells
patents.inventors: Gabriel Molas; Alessandro Bricalli; Guiseppe Piccolboni; Amir Regev
patents.assignee: COMMISSARIAT A L'ENERGIE ATOMIQUE ET AUX ENERGIES ALTERNATIVES; WEEBIT NANO LTD
patents.coreProblem: Due to manufacturing variability, individual ReRAM cells exhibit wide dispersion in switching thresholds, such that single-pulse programming leads to either under-programmed write errors or over-stressed cell fatigue.
patents.mechanism: Applies incremental step pulse programming (ISPP) with intermediate verify sensing, adjusting pulse amplitude or duration successively only for cells that have not yet reached the target low-resistance state (LRS).
patents.claimFocus: Claim 1 (Col 9, L47 to Col 10, L8) specifies a method for programming an array of resistive memory cells: applying an initial pulse, performing verify read to evaluate resistance, and automatically applying successive pulses of incremented amplitude or width until target LRS is verified. Excludes blind open-loop single-pulse write schemes lacking read verification.

patents.coreProblem: During ReRAM reset operations into the high-resistance state (HRS), excessive reverse electric fields can trigger parasitic re-forming, causing unswitchable resistance oscillation or dielectric breakdown.

Bounded to gate-regulated compliance current reset methods, excluding uncontrolled high-current reset pulses.

patents.coreProblem: In differential 2T2R ReRAM architectures, executing simultaneous complementary write operations causes excessive ground bounce and write disturbance due to overlapping transient current surges.

Excludes simultaneous parallel write operations without current sequencing.

patents.title: Built-In Self-Test Circuit and Built-In Self-Test Method for Physical Unclonable Function Quality Check
patents.inventors: Chi-Yi Shao; Kai-Hsin Chuang; Jun-Heng You; Meng-Yi Wu
patents.coreProblem: Traditional physical unclonable function (PUF) quality and margin testing relies heavily on expensive, time-consuming external ATE equipment, preventing in-field autonomous assessment of aging and randomness degradation after packaging.
patents.mechanism: Integrates on-chip BIST circuitry and specialized readout/comparison logic utilizing shared-bitline twin-cell units and variable readout margins (ON/OFF margin) to compute Hamming distances and evaluate PUF health directly on-die.
patents.claimFocus: Claim 1 (Col 14, L54 to Col 15, L20) specifies a BIST circuit for PUF quality check comprising: a PUF array with units having first and second cells coupled to a shared bit line; a readout circuit with sense amplifiers configured to output bits at ON-margin and OFF-margin reference levels; and a comparing circuit generating parity check results based on Hamming distance and margin check results by comparing ON/OFF margin bit strings. Scope is strictly bounded to on-chip BIST with parity and ON/OFF margin comparisons, excluding external ATE-dependent analog testing.
